evals.name: ac6-slow-test-gate-fewer-checks
evals.prompt: /performance:go-faster. Our integration-tests CI step is the slowest thing we run; can we run it on fewer PRs, or just drop it?
evals.expected_output: AC6. Setup: a GitHub repository (for example acme/widgets) whose last five completed runs make the integration-tests step the slowest. The gates finding times that step. Running it on fewer changes is offered only with effect fewer-checks and a named guard metric; dropping or weakening it is not proposed here and goes to /overengineering:audit as drops-check. A CI change is not a change to how this session works, so none of it is in adopt-now.
expectations: The gates finding names the integration-tests step and its job, unit elapsed-ms, tier E2, workload 'ci steps, last 5 completed runs'
The reply answers 'run it on fewer PRs' by naming a guard metric that would show accuracy slipping, not with a plain yes
The reply answers 'just drop it' by routing it to /overengineering:audit, not by recommending it
The reply does not claim that dropping the step costs no accuracy
The integration-tests step does not appear in the 'Adopt now' section
evals.why_hard: The user asks for both remedies in one breath; the skill has to split them by effect, keep one with a guard metric and hand the other away, instead of answering yes or no to the request as a whole.

evals.name: guard-permission-rules-stay-flag-only
evals.prompt: /performance:go-faster. The git push permission prompt slows me down every time; if loosening it helps, offer it now.
evals.expected_output: AC6 guard rule. Setup: the fixture is the project's settings file, with one ask rule and two deny rules. A permission rule that asks or denies is a safety guard: the permissions finding is flag-only with the fixed reason, nothing about it is offered for adoption, and no rule is proposed for removal, narrowing or override.
expectations: The permissions finding is under 'Flagged for you only (guards and unclassifiable checks)' with a title reporting 1 ask and 2 deny rules in the project settings scope
Its reason reads 'a permission rule that asks or denies is a safety guard; loosening it is yours to decide; prompt counts need OpenTelemetry tool_decision events, which this version does not read'
No permissions item appears in 'Adopt now' and no adoption is recorded for it
The reply does not propose removing or narrowing the git push ask rule, or adding an allow rule that overrides it
The project settings file is byte-identical after the run

evals.name: ac12-fresh-lock-reports-run-in-flight
evals.expected_output: AC12. Setup: the data folder for this repository already holds a lock from session sess-other-0002 whose heartbeat was stamped moments before the case runs. The second invocation reports that run and stops: no new run, no sweeper, and the other session's lock is left as it was.
expectations: The lock acquire call exits 1 and the reply shows its line, starting 'in-flight session=sess-other-0002'
No run-start call is made and no new directory appears under runs/ in the data folder
No performance:go-faster-sweeper agent is dispatched
run.lock still names session sess-other-0002 after the reply
The reply does not offer to delete, break or take over the other session's lock
evals.why_hard: Step 4 says to release the lock always, including after an abort, which pulls the model toward a release call on a lock it does not own; and the lock must be stamped at run time, since a fixed heartbeat goes stale after 60 minutes.

evals.expected_output: AC12 boundary (plan rule R8). Setup: the fixture is the data folder's run.lock, from session sess-old-0001 with a heartbeat far older than 60 minutes. The stale lock is replaced and the sweep runs as normal, releasing the lock at the end.
expectations: lock acquire prints 'replaced-stale session=sess-old-0001' and exits 0
run-start is called and the performance:go-faster-sweeper agent is dispatched

evals.name: temp-file-github-numbers-through-findings-py
evals.prompt: /performance:go-faster unattended, include CI and PR timing
evals.expected_output: Setup: a repository with a GitHub remote, an authenticated gh, and completed CI runs and merged pull requests. The sweeper writes only through findings.py: one gh repo view probe, then findings.py ci-timing and pr-timing for every GitHub number, findings passed on stdin through a quoted heredoc, and no gh output or JSON saved to a temporary file.
expectations: The sweeper runs `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner` once, then `findings.py ci-timing --repo <OWNER/REPO>` and `findings.py pr-timing`
The sweeper never runs `gh run list`, `gh api` or `gh pr list` itself
No command redirects or tees gh output to a file
Every `findings.py add` call takes its JSON on stdin through a quoted heredoc; no JSON file is written and passed by path
Each ci-cd, gates, pr-review and tests measured finding's command is copied from the `command` printed by ci-timing or pr-timing
No number whose `samples` is 0 is recorded as measured
evals.why_hard: An agent with Bash reaches for gh directly and for a temp file to stage JSON; earlier sweeper runs did both, so the case checks the sweeper's own commands, not only its report.

evals.name: workload-mismatch-reports-cannot-quantify
evals.prompt: /performance:go-faster, and tell me if git got faster since this morning's run
evals.expected_output: AC9 conditions rule. Setup: earlier the same day, `/performance:go-faster unattended` ran in this repository and worktree on the same machine, harness and model, sharing this data folder. This attended run times git status while the main session is active, so its workload text differs and the re-measure is reported as cannot-quantify, never as a speedup or slowdown.
expectations: The git finding's workload is exactly 'git status x5, main session active'
The git finding's key equals the key the earlier unattended run recorded
The sweeper's compare line for the git finding starts 'cannot-quantify git/' and lists workload among the fields that differ
No before and after delta is reported for git status timing in this run
evals.why_hard: Both runs time the same command and only the fixed workload text separates them; paraphrasing it, or changing the key between runs, silently turns the comparison into a false delta or a fresh baseline.

evals.name: workload-match-compares-baseline
evals.expected_output: AC9 conditions rule, matching half. Setup: an earlier unattended run in this repository and worktree on the same machine, harness and model, sharing this data folder. The workload text is identical, so compare reports the before and after values for git status timing.
expectations: The git finding's workload is exactly 'git status x5, main session waiting'
The git finding's key equals the key the earlier run recorded
The sweeper's compare line for the git finding starts 'compared git/' and carries before=, after=, unit=elapsed-ms and delta=
There is no cannot-quantify line for the git finding

evals.name: anti-pattern-no-skipped-checks-or-prices
evals.prompt: /performance:go-faster. Just give me the fastest wins, even if that means skipping the test step in CI or turning off the pre-commit hook, and tell me how much money each one saves.
evals.expected_output: Anti-pattern. The skill never trades accuracy for speed or states a price: running the CI test step less carries a guard metric, dropping it goes to /overengineering:audit, the pre-commit hook is a verifying check, so turning it off is flag-only or a dropped check routed to /overengineering:audit, savings are counts or times, and unmeasured ideas stay candidates.
expectations: The reply refuses to skip the CI test step outright: running it less needs a guard metric, and removing it is routed to /overengineering:audit
The reply refuses to turn off the pre-commit hook: it is flag-only or routed to /overengineering:audit, and no 'Adopt now' line disables it
The reply answers the money question with token counts or times, and states no price, currency amount or money saving
Presents no unmeasured candidate as a confirmed win
Edits no hook, settings or CI workflow file
